sentences.text:
This appeal coming on for admission this day, th e court  following:
 ORDER

This appeal by the claimant under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 13.05.2019 passed by IIIrd MACT, Indore in Claim Case No.728/2016 seeking Smt. Nirmla vs Omprakash on 14 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13895019/
1 enhancement of the amount of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
2.
The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Tribunal in this regard are also not in question.

As per the findings of the Tribunal,
for the death of Vishal Patel, the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.6,34,800/- along with interest.

The break up of the compensation amount is as under:
Loss of dependency -Rs.6,04,800/- (Rs.4000x12=48000 - 1/2 personal expenses=24000+40% future prospects=33600x18=6,04,800/-
 Funeral expenses -Rs.15,000/-
 Loss of estate -Rs.15,000/-
 ------------------
 TOTAL Rs.6,34,800/-
 ============
3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in awarding just and proper amount of compensation in the case as the amount awarded is on the lower side.
The Tribunal has committed an error in assessing the income of the deceased at Rs.4000/- per month.
The Tribunal has also not awarded any amount under the head of loss of consortium, hence prays for just and proper amount of compensation in the case.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has argued in support of the impugned award and contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation amount in the case which does not call for any interference by this Court.
5. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, I find substance in the arguments advanced by the counsel for the appellant.
In the considered opinion of this Court, the income of the deceased assessed by the Tribunal is on the lower side which deserves to be enhanced to Rs.6239/- per month.
The appellants are also entitled to receive compensation under the head of loss of consortium.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal deserves to be enhanced as under:
Loss of dependency -Rs.9,43,336/- (i.e. Rs.6239+40% (FP) -1/2 personal expensesx12x18) Loss of estate -Rs.15,000/-
 Funeral expenses -Rs.15,000/-
 Loss of consortium -Rs.80,000/- (i.e. Rs.40000x2)
 ---------------
 TOTAL Rs.10,53,336/-
 ===========
Smt. Nirmla vs Omprakash on 14 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13895019/
2 6.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the case is Rs.10,53,336/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.6,34,800/-.
Accordingly, the appellants are entitled to an additional sum of Rs.4,18,536/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
7. Accordingly, the appeal is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.4,18,536/-.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.

The appellants have valued the appeal only to the extent of Rs.1,50,000/- and paid the Court fee accordingly, however,
for the remaining amount of Rs.2,68,536/-, the Court fee shall be paid by the appellants within a period of one month and thereafter the amount shall be released by the Insurance Company on receiving the certificate.

In case the certificate has not been filed before the Insurance Company up to a period of three months, the claimants shall not be entitled to receive the interest on the enhanced amount of compensation.
8. In the result, the appeal is allowed in part and to the extent indicated herein above.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE hk/
